transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Yeah… I’m here because the clinic for a logistics job said my weight was too low to clear me. I don’t really see it that way. I look lean, I guess—like I can move quick and do the work.
Do you think your weight is too low?
Not really. I mean… my sister and the doctor keep saying it’s dangerous, but I think they’re making more of it than it is. I’m just trying to stay light and sharp, you know, ready for work.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I don’t know if I’d call it afraid. I just… if I eat rice or bread, or greasy stuff, it gets in my head that it’s going to stick to me right away. Then I’ll check the scale, or my belt, the next morning… just to make sure I didn’t let myself go.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I guess… yeah, maybe. It’s more like if I eat rice or bread, or something greasy, I can’t stop thinking it’ll sit on me right away. Then I end up checking the scale or my belt the next morning, just to make sure I didn’t let myself go.
Do you think you look too thin when you look in the mirror?
Not really too thin. I mean… I look at my stomach, my waist mostly. If it’s not smaller, kind of tight-looking, I feel like I’m slipping… like I’m not the disciplined guy I used to be at work.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I mean… they said it was significant. The clinic for the logistics job wouldn’t clear me because my weight was too low. I don’t really see it that way—I just look lean, like I can still move quick and work.
Have you had your menstrual period in the past few months?
Uh… no. I mean, I’m a man, so I don’t have periods.
Do you often limit the amount of food you eat because you're worried about gaining weight?
Yeah… I guess I do. Most days it’s just black coffee, maybe a boiled egg or some tuna. If I’m not moving freight that day, I tell myself I don’t really need a full meal.
Do you think your weight or body shape is the same as how others see you

Not really. People say I’m too thin, but when I look… mostly at my stomach and waist, I just see places that could be tighter. Smaller. If I don’t keep that, I feel like I’m not the disciplined guy I used to be at work.
Do you think you would be less disciplined or less capable at your job if you gained a small amount of weight?

Yeah… I think so. If I put on weight, even a little, I feel like I’m getting soft. When I look in the mirror, especially around my stomach and waist, it’s like… if I’m not smaller and tight-looking, then I’m not the same disciplined guy I was on the warehouse floor.
Do you think your body shape or weight is normal when others tell you it's not?

I mean… I don’t think it’s as bad as they’re saying. My sister and the doctor keep telling me I’m in danger, but… I think they’re making it bigger than it is. I’m just trying to stay light, sharp, ready for work.
Are you ever worried that if you start eating, you won't be able to stop?
I don’t know… not really. I guess I haven’t thought about it like that. I’m more just careful with what I eat.
When you look at yourself, do you see yourself as others describe you?

Not really. I mean… I see what they’re pointing at, but when I look, it’s more my stomach and waist. If I don’t look smaller and tight there, I feel like I’m not… the disciplined guy I used to be at work.
Do you think your body shape or weight is the same as how it actually is, regardless of what others say?
I don’t know if it’s the same. When I look, I mostly notice my stomach and waist… and if I’m not smaller, tight-looking, I feel like I’m not the disciplined man I used to be on the warehouse floor.
Do you think your body shape or weight is the main thing that makes you who you are?

I don’t know if it’s the main thing… but yeah, it feels tied up in it. When I look at my stomach or waist, if I don’t look smaller and tight, I feel like I’m not the disciplined guy I used to be at work.
When you look at yourself, do you see a different body shape than what you think others see?

Yeah… I guess I do. Other people seem to see me one way, but when I look in the mirror, I’m stuck on my stomach and waist. If it doesn’t look smaller and tight, I just… don’t feel like that disciplined guy I was on the warehouse floor.
Do you think your weight or body shape would affect your identity or self-worth if it changed?
Yeah… I think it would. If my stomach or waist changes and I don’t look smaller, tight… I feel like I’m not really that disciplined man I used to be. Like I’ve lost something about myself.
Do you think you would look okay if you gained a little weight
Honestly… no, I don’t think I would. If I gained weight, I’d see it in my stomach and waist, and I’d feel like I wasn’t that disciplined man I used to be.
